da-non-sequitur.evidence: S↔P: Step 1 is false for the Kazhdan–Lusztig bar involution. The prf claims "bar(e_λ) = e_{λ'}" (prf:8-9). Exact counterexample in H_2 (balanced convention, σ⁻¹ = σ − h): e_(2) = (σ + q⁻¹)/(q + q⁻¹). Under bar (q ↦ q⁻¹, σ ↦ σ⁻¹) it maps to (σ − h + q)/(q⁻¹ + q) = (σ + q⁻¹)/(q + q⁻¹) = e_(2), not e_(1,1) (sympy difference 0). The bar involution fixes every e_λ; the involution that transposes λ is the Goldman/sign-type σ ↦ −σ⁻¹ (or its composite with bar), which the prf does not name. Steps 2-3 are heuristic pairings with no definition of "pairing with a depth-n grouplike" (prf:31-57; "non-by definition" at prf:36, 49 is garbled). d_II is defined only through conj:two-filtration-bridge (md:9-10), so the "theorem-level" claim for all partitions (md:3-4, ts tag "theorem-level") rests on a conjecture plus a false step.

trap-superlative.evidence: SWEEP DAMAGE, and it lands on the load-bearing step of the proof. The phrase "non-by definition" appears twice, as the verdict of two pairing computations: "At $n = 2$: pairs with Vol (bar-fixed) --- non-by definition." and "Bar-antisymmetric: $(e_\lambda - e_{\lambda'})/2$ --- pairs with depth-3 (CS-type) periods non-by definition." A third site in the same paragraph reads "The bar-symmetric part pairs by definition with depth-2 of a chiral knot", where "by definition" is doing no work and the sentence's own continuation ("volume can be non-zero, but ...") suggests the original said something about non-vanishing. This is the documented "non-by definition" garble class; at all three sites the substituted token IS the conclusion of the step - whether a pairing vanishes or not - so the proof's two key inferences currently read as nonsense.
